c.tagline: Ancient Song-dynasty capital of iron pagodas and night-market food.

taxi.fareNote: Metered from about ¥6-8; short hops across the compact old city are cheap. Pay by Alipay/WeChat or cash.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police, 120 an ambulance, and 119 the fire service; there is no single combined emergency number, and 112 works from mobiles to route you.

hood_landmark.Shunhe Hui District: Iron Pagoda (Tieta) and its park, Kaifeng

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the packed Gulou night market and use metered or app-hailed taxis rather than touts.

hood_desc: Kaifeng's downtown heart around the rebuilt Drum Tower and the Gulou Night Market, a maze of snack stalls, teahouses, and shops; the liveliest and most convenient base for first-timers who want the city's famous street food on their doorstep.

The historic north end of the old city around Longting (Dragon Pavilion) Park and its twin lakes, with the Song Imperial Street running south from the palace gate and the Millennium City Park recreating a Song-era townscape just to the west; Kaifeng at its grandest, all palaces, gates and water.

Kaifeng's Hui Muslim district, named for the community that lives here, spreading northeast of the old centre; it takes in the thousand-year-old Iron Pagoda and its park at Tieta, along with quiet residential lanes, mosques and halal food. Atmospheric and local rather than polished.

Kaifeng's newer western district beyond the old walls, built around the broad Kaifeng Xihu (Bianxi) Lake and the Zhengkai Avenue corridor running toward Zhengzhou; wide roads, most of the city's international-brand hotels and quiet, green surroundings a short ride from the old city.
A calm southern district named for King Yu's Terrace (Yuwangtai Park), an ancient earthen platform amid gardens; a quiet, local, budget-friendly area away from the tourist crush.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water; tap water is not potable.

transit.hours: City buses and BRT lines run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM; there is no metro.
transit.note: Kaifeng has no metro; the compact old city is served by an extensive city bus network (including Bus Rapid Transit lines) plus taxis and DiDi, and most Song-era sights are within walking distance or a short ride apart.
transit.pay: Pay by scanning an Alipay or WeChat Pay QR code, tapping a rechargeable transit card, or cash (exact change, flat ¥1-2 fare) on board.

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in China; no service charge or gratuity is needed at restaurants, hotels, or taxis.

food.name: Guantang Baozi (soup dumplings)
food.desc: Kaifeng's famous xiaolongbao, pleated in exactly 32 folds and filled with pork and hot aspic broth; the Song-era ancestor of Shanghai's soup dumpling.

places.name: Diyilou (First Floor) Baozi Restaurant
places.area: Sihou Street, by the Drum Tower
places.note: The state-recognised China Time-Honoured Brand that made the dumpling famous; the reference version.

places.name: Huangjia Laodian
places.area: Jinan Road, with a branch on Song Imperial Street
places.note: Founded by a former Diyilou master; locals rate the filling generous and the price fairer.

places.name: Lao Huang Ji
places.area: City centre near the Drum Tower
places.note: The third of Kaifeng's big three soup-dumpling houses; busy with residents at lunch.

food.name: Chao Liangfen (stir-fried jelly)
food.desc: Mung-bean jelly cubes fried on a huge flat griddle with garlic, chilli and bean paste until the edges crisp and the middle turns molten.

places.name: Gulou Night Market
places.note: The classic tourist night market; go for the theatre of the griddles after dark.

places.name: Xisi Night Market
places.area: Xisi Square, west of the centre
places.note: Where Kaifeng residents actually eat; cheaper and less geared to visitors.

places.name: Wuyi Night Market
places.note: Neighbourhood night market with a strong run of griddle and grill stalls.

food.name: Huasheng Gao (peanut cake)
food.desc: Crumbly slab of ground roasted peanuts and malt sugar that dissolves on the tongue; Kaifeng's best-known sweet and the standard souvenir.

places.name: Xingshengde
places.note: The historic peanut cake maker in Kaifeng; the benchmark brand for the sweet.

places.name: Gulou Night Market
places.note: Stalls sell it warm and freshly cut rather than boxed.

places.name: Song Imperial Street shops
places.area: Songdu Yujie, north of the Drum Tower
places.note: Row of speciality shops selling Kaifeng sweets and preserved goods.

food.name: Tongzi Ji (barrel chicken)
food.desc: Whole chicken poached in an aromatic master stock until the skin glows amber and the meat stays firm and cool; sliced and eaten as a cold starter.

places.name: Ma Yuxing Tongzi Ji
places.note: Qing dynasty halal brand that created the dish; the name locals buy for gifts.

places.name: Youyixin Restaurant
places.note: Old-established halal restaurant serving the classic Kaifeng cold dishes.

places.name: Gulou Night Market
places.note: Vendors sell it sliced by weight to eat with beer.

food.name: Liyu Beimian (carp with fine noodles)
food.desc: Yellow River carp in sweet-and-sour sauce, crowned with a nest of hair-thin fried noodles that you press into the sauce; a Song banquet centrepiece.

places.name: Youyixin Restaurant
places.note: One of the old restaurants that keeps the full Kaifeng banquet repertoire.

places.name: Kaifeng Restaurant (Kaifeng Fandian)
places.note: State-era dining hall known for classic Henan banquet cooking.

places.name: Bianjing Restaurant
places.note: Traditional house doing Yellow River carp for group tables; order ahead.

food.name: Guotie and Kang Mo (griddle snacks)
food.desc: Rows of pan-fried pork dumplings with lacy crisp bottoms, plus kang mo, flatbread pressed onto the griddle with cumin-spiced mutton.

places.name: Xingjia Guotie
places.note: Long-standing dumpling shop that locals name before any of the night markets.

places.name: Daoxiangju
places.note: Time-honoured Kaifeng brand for pan-fried dumplings and steamed snacks.

places.name: Xisi Night Market
places.area: Xisi Square, west of the centre
places.note: Best place for mutton kang mo cooked to order on open griddles.

food.name: Xingren Cha (almond tea)
food.desc: Hot, silky almond and rice gruel poured from a long-spouted copper kettle and topped with nuts, raisins and osmanthus; a night market ritual.

places.name: Gulou Night Market
places.note: Copper kettle stalls pour it theatrically; the signature drink of the market.

places.name: Xisi Night Market
places.area: Xisi Square, west of the centre
places.note: Same drink at local prices, usually with a shorter queue.

places.name: Song Imperial Street stalls
places.area: Songdu Yujie, north of the Drum Tower
places.note: Sold along the recreated Song street, best on a cold evening.

food.name: Siwei Leicha (four-flavour tea)
food.desc: Kaifeng night market oddity: a savoury-sweet broth of sesame, peanut, ginger and herbs, thickened and sipped hot from a small bowl.

places.name: Gulou Night Market
places.note: A handful of stalls specialise in it; look for the tall stacked bowls.

places.name: Xisi Night Market
places.area: Xisi Square, west of the centre
places.note: Local market where the older stallholders still make it the traditional way.

places.name: Wuyi Night Market
places.note: Neighbourhood option away from the tourist crowds.

landmarks: Millennium City Park (Qingming Riverside Landscape Garden)
A sprawling living recreation of the famous 'Along the River During Qingming' scroll, with Song-dynasty boats, acrobats, and costumed street scenes daily.
Iron Pagoda (Tie Ta)
A 55-meter octagonal pagoda from 1049 clad in iron-hued glazed tiles, it has survived floods, earthquakes and wars for nearly a millennium.
Dragon Pavilion (Longting Park)
A towering Qing-dynasty pavilion on the site of Northern Song imperial palaces, rising over twin lakes at the head of Kaifeng's royal axis.
Daxiangguo Temple
One of ancient China's most celebrated Buddhist monasteries, founded in 555 AD, famed for its octagonal pavilion sheltering a four-faced thousand-hand Guanyin carved from gingko.
Kaifeng Fu (Ancient Government Office)
A faithful reconstruction of the Northern Song municipal court where legendary Judge Bao dispensed justice, staging daily gate-opening ceremonies and courtroom dramas.
Lord Bao Memorial Temple (Baogong Ci)
A serene lakeside shrine honoring Bao Zheng, China's incorruptible Song-dynasty judge, whose black-faced image still symbolizes justice across Asia.
Shanshangan Guild Hall
A lavish Qing-dynasty merchants' guild hall whose brick, wood and stone carvings of auspicious scenes rank among central China's most exuberant craftsmanship.
Gulou (Drum Tower) Night Market
Kaifeng's legendary night market floods the drum tower square with steaming five-spice buns, sesame soup dumplings and the city's signature carry-on chicken.
Po Pagoda (Fan Pagoda)
Kaifeng's oldest surviving structure, a stout brick pagoda from 977 AD, every surface stamped with intricate Buddha-image tiles in quiet backstreets.
Kaifeng Ancient City Wall
China's second-longest surviving city wall loops 14 kilometers around old Kaifeng, its Qing-era ramparts concealing flood-buried cities stacked beneath.

train.note: Kaifeng has no international trains. Three stations serve the city: Kaifeng station on the old Longhai line, with about 6.5 hours from Shanghai (¥222), 7 hours from Xi'an (¥140) and 45 minutes from Zhengzhou (¥11-19); Songchenglu station, from which intercity high-speed trains reach Zhengzhou East in 30 minutes and continue to Xinzheng airport roughly every 90 minutes; and Kaifeng North on the Lanzhou-Xuzhou high-speed line. Hard seats can be hard to come by on the Longhai trains, but next-day or even same-day hard sleepers are often available. Book on 12306 with your passport.

bus.note: No international coaches serve Kaifeng. Kaifeng Central Bus Station near Kaifeng railway station is the main terminal, with buses from Zhengzhou Long-Distance Bus Station and Luoyang Long-Distance Bus Station plus longer runs to Shanghai, Beijing and Guangzhou. Tickets are bought at the counters, but for the short hop to Zhengzhou the intercity train from Songchenglu is faster and more frequent than the bus.

ferry.note: Kaifeng has no passenger ferry services. The Yellow River passes a few kilometres north of the city but is shallow, silted and unnavigable for scheduled boats; the riverbank at Liuyuankou is a viewpoint with local sightseeing craft only.

half.name: Zhengzhou Yellow River Scenic Area
half.blurb: Cable cars and viewing platforms overlook the point where the Yellow River exits its mountain course onto the North China Plain.

half.name: Longmen Grottoes, Luoyang
half.blurb: Thousands of Buddhist statues carved into limestone cliffs along the Yi River date back more than 1,500 years to the Northern Wei dynasty.

half.name: Shaolin Temple, Dengfeng
half.blurb: The birthplace of Shaolin kung fu sits at the foot of Mount Song, with a forest of stone stupas marking monks' burial sites nearby.
